old_title: Ukraine war latest: US envoys set to meet Zelensky after 'highly useful' Putin talks
new_title: Ukraine live: Trump's envoys confronted over holding talks with 'war criminal' Putin
old_text:
Russian president Vladimir Putin held more than three hours of talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow as Donald Trump's administration stepped up efforts to broker an end to the Ukraine war.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the talks were "substantive, constructive and extremely frank", but he gave no indication of any breakthrough.
He added that "the negotiations were timely and highly useful for both sides". He said the US envoys "outlined a number of ideas regarding possible avenues for a settlement", while Putin "reaffirmed Russia's readiness to continue working with the US to find a political and diplomatic solution" to the conflict.
Putin told the envoys that Russia was making "real progress" on the battlefield, and that "all the root causes of the conflict" needed to be addressed.
Witkoff and Kushner have since left Moscow and are due to meet Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv on Sunday.
Putin said he had ordered Russian forces to halt strikes on Kyiv after receiving a request through diplomatic and intelligence channels, while Ukraine has said it will similarly refrain from striking Moscow through Monday.
Zelensky says Russia deliberately targeted Kyiv airports ahead of US visit
Russia struck Kyiv's Zhuliany and Boryspil airports overnight on Friday and Saturday, in what president Volodymyr Zelensky said was a deliberate response to preparations for US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner potentially flying into Ukraine.
"Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine and land at Kyiv Airport or Boryspil Airport," Zelensky said. He said Ukraine had recorded the move and would adjust its operations concerning Russian airspace the following week.
The overnight attacks also damaged a nine-storey residential building in Boryspil, where two women were injured, while fires were reported in the Kyiv region. The strikes came hours before Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow; the pair are due to travel to Kyiv on Sunday.
India ready to help end Russia-Ukraine war, says foreign minister on visit to Kyiv
India is ready to help bring an end to the Russia-Ukraine war, the country's external affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Thursday during his visit to Kyiv.
"If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there," he said, standing alongside his Ukrainian counterpart Andrii Sybiha, Reuters reported.
The foreign minister's visit to Kyiv comes just days after Indian prime minister Narendra Modi met Russian president Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan on Monday.
Russia's wartime budget deficit reaches 2.8 per cent of GDP
Russia's budget deficit increased by 40 per cent between January and July to 2.8 per cent of GDP, as the cost of its war in Ukraine continues to weigh on government finances, Vladimir Putin said on Thursday.
The official target for the full year is 1.6 per cent of GDP, with Moscow relying on higher taxes and borrowing to help finance spending.
Putin dismissed concerns over the widening deficit, saying: "Considering that we have one of the lowest levels of national debt in the world, there is nothing critical here." He said Russia would manage the shortfall despite the deterioration in its finances.
Russia shifts tactics with round-the-clock attacks on Kyiv, disrupting daily life
G7 and IMF assess Ukraine's finances as war strains economy
G7 ambassadors in Kyiv have met an International Monetary Fund mission led by Gavin Gray to discuss Ukraine's economic outlook, with the G7 saying reforms aligned with EU standards remain a priority.
The IMF mission began meetings on 31 August and is examining Ukraine's macroeconomic policies and reforms under its four-year, $8.1bn Extended Fund Facility, as well as the draft 2027 budget.
Ukraine's $8.1bn four-year IMF programme remains a key source of international financing. The IMF approved a $690m disbursement in July, taking total payments under the programme to about $2.2bn, but said the economic outlook had weakened because of intensified Russian attacks on critical infrastructure and spillovers from the Middle East war.
ICYMI: Putin meets Trump envoys as limited truce takes effect
Russian president Vladimir Putin held more than three hours of talks with Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow on Saturday, with Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov describing the meeting as "substantive, very frank, and constructive".
Ushakov said the envoys "put forward a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement" and would take Putin's views to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv.
A White House official said the sides had discussed "substantive plans for next steps", to be announced in the coming weeks.
Putin told the envoys Russia was making "real progress" on the battlefield and insisted that "all the root causes of the conflict" had to be addressed. At the start of the meeting, he asked them to convey his "very best wishes and words of gratitude" to Trump, saying the US president was continuing efforts to resolve the conflict despite "a difficult situation".
The talks took place during a limited pause in strikes on the two capitals. Putin said he had ordered Russian forces not to strike Kyiv for three days after receiving a request through diplomatic and intelligence channels, saying: "I issued the relevant order, and no strikes have been carried out on Kyiv since midnight."
Zelensky said Ukraine would refrain from striking Moscow through Monday.
Germany once cosied up to Putin. Now they are Russia's public enemy number one in Europe
Norway seizes Russian vessel over $4.2bn Ukraine claim
Norway seized a Russian research vessel in Svalbard on Wednesday at the request of Ukraine's state-owned energy company Naftogaz, as part of efforts to enforce a $4.22bn arbitration award over Russia's seizure of Ukrainian energy assets in Crimea.
An arbitration tribunal in The Hague ordered Russia to pay the sum in 2023, but Moscow has refused to do so.
The vessel, the Professor Molchanov, was seized after Naftogaz sought enforcement through Norwegian courts. The company has been pursuing Russian commercial assets in several countries as it tries to recover the award stemming from Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea.
US NATO envoy calls Leipzig drone attack 'more concerning'
NATO's US ambassador Matthew Whitaker has described an attempted Russian-linked drone attack at a German airport as a concerning example of Moscow's alleged hybrid warfare against Europe.
A drone carrying explosives was found in a restricted area at Leipzig on 4 August, near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft. The device failed to detonate, but its discovery forced the closure of a runway and disrupted flights.
German authorities later found traces of military explosives and concluded that Russia was behind the attempted attack, saying individuals involved had acted on behalf of Russian state agencies.
"Then you have what I would call the more concerning hybrid actions, as we saw in Leipzig, as we have seen in Poland," Whitaker said on Saturday. "If we can identify who's doing it - which Germany did - we make sure we express strongly that is unacceptable and we will not tolerate it."
Russia has denied involvement. Germany has said it will close Russia's consulate in Bonn and the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin in response to the incident.
Russian oil refinery hit as Ukraine launches overnight drone barrage
Ukrainian drones targeted an oil refinery in Ryazan and several cities across Russia overnight, with explosions reported in Rostov-on-Don and a child injured in the southern city.
Rostov region governor Yuri Slyusar said air defences destroyed around 30 drones over the region. Two apartment buildings in Rostov-on-Don were damaged and a child was hospitalised, while damage was also reported to homes in other parts of the region, according to the Kyiv Independent.
An oil refinery in Ryazan was also targeted, with a fire reported at the site. The plant, which accounts for about 5 per cent of Russia's refining capacity, has previously been hit by Ukrainian drones and suffered an operational shutdown in July.
new_text:
Donald Trump's peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have been confronted over their talks with "war criminal" Russian president Vladimir Putin.
In a news conference in Kyiv alongside Volodymry Zelensky on Sunday, Ukrainian journalist Dmytro Gordon asked whether Putin was deceiving the US president.
"You have met with President Putin very often. Does it seem to you that Putin has been deceiving you all this time?," he added according to the Kyiv Post.
"And finally, don't you find it disgusting to sit at the same table with an international war criminal, the executioner of the Ukrainian people, who is personally responsible for the tragedy in Ukraine?" he added.
Zelensky held talks with Witkoff and Kushner on Sunday, after their three-hour talks with Putin in Moscow on Saturday. He lauded their "very substantive" conversation and said Ukraine was ready for trilateral talks involving Russia, the US and Ukraine.
The US president is expected to speak to Putin and Zelensky over the phone on Monday.
Meanwhile, Kyiv's air raid alerts have reached their highest level since the war began in February 2022, as Russia ramps up its targeting of the Ukrainian capital, according to an analysis of government figures by BBC Verify.
Putin meets with Kushner and Witkoff amid Ukraine war peace talks - ICYMI
Zelensky says oil refinery hit in Ryazan region
Volodymyr Zelensky has said a Russian oil refinery in the Ryazan region was struck by Ukrainian drones in a fresh long-range attack.
"Our warriors continue responding justly to Russian strikes on Ukraine. An oil refinery was hit in the Ryazan region," the Ukrainian president said, sharing footage which he said was of the strike.
"Our long-range capabilities were used against oil-processing facilities in the Perm region and Tatarstan, and against a site used to store and launch attack drones in the Kursk region," he added.
"A target was also hit in the Black Sea. I thank every one of our units for their precision!"
Kyiv air raid alerts hit record high - report
Air raid alerts in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv are at their highest levels of the war so far, as Russia ramps up attacks on the Ukrainian capital, according to a report.
Moscow's new strategy of increasing daytime attacks on the city has forced it to drive up the frequency of its daily air raid alerts, BBC Verify reported in an analysis of Ukrainian government figures.
Residents have been forced to head to the shelters as often as 13 times a day, the analysis said.
'Overnight we all became war correspondents': Ukraine's local newspapers face battle to stay alive
In the weeks leading up to Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine, the headlines in a Kyiv newspaper looked much like they would anywhere else.
There was some debate over whether Russia would actually attack its neighbour. But then, outside of politics, there was everything else: the tourists stuck abroad, changes to school meals and the spread of the Omicron variant of Covid.
On 24 February 2022, everything changed as Russian tanks rolled across the border. Businesses closed or relocated, martial law saw hundreds of thousands of working-age men recruited for military service, and around one million people fled the country in the first week.
A brave few stayed behind to keep a record of what happened as the missiles rained down. Local journalists observed and asked questions as their communities were torn apart by the war.
Industrial facility damaged in Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Tatarstan region
An industrial facility sustained minor damage in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Tatarstan region on the Volga river, the state-run TASS news agency reported on Monday, citing the regional governor's press service.
The news agency has not identified the facility or specified its location.
Eleven dead and six missing after avalanche in Russian mountains
The avalanche hit a group of climbers in the Kabardino-Balkaria region in the North Caucasus on Sunday.
It swept down Mount Mizhirgi, one of the area's highest peaks, around 5pm local time (2pm GMT), hitting a group of 33 climbers, emergency services said.
Ten climbers had made their own way down the mountain as of 9am local time on Monday.
Russia launches 92 drones at Ukraine, says Kyiv's air force
Russian forces have attacked Ukraine with 92 drones overnight into Monday, the Ukrainian air force has said in its daily update.
Kyiv's air force shot down or jammed 71 of the drones, while 12 locations were struck, it said.
Aircraft, anti-aircraft missile units, and electronic warfare was used to down the drones, the force said in the Telegram update.
As of 7am BST it said the attack was ongoing.
Trump to speak with Putin and Zelensky on Monday
Donald Trump is set to hold phone calls with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday, according to a report.
The US president will first speak with the Russian president before speaking to Mr Zelensky, after he is briefed by his envoys on their latest talks with Russian and Ukrainian negotiators, a report in The Kyiv Independent said.
The US envoys arrived in Kyiv by train on 6 September where they were met by Mr Zelensky at Sofiiska Square, before they engaged in negotiations.
Russia and North Korea open new bridge over Tumen river
North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge on Monday, Russia's TASS state news agency reported.
The structure spans the Tumen river and is located near the "Friendship Bridge", a rail bridge commissioned in 1959 after the Korean war.
There are already direct air and rail links between Moscow and Pyongyang, who have described the new bridge as yet another milestone in their growing strategic partnership.
Russian prime minister Mikhail Mishustin said the bridge should spur development between the two countries in various spheres - including tourism - and create new jobs.
"I am convinced that the expansion of cross-border transport infrastructure will provide a powerful impetus for the further development of trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation," TASS cited Mishustin as saying at the bridge's opening ceremony via video link.
Construction of the new bridge, which had been under discussion for years, began in April last year after its construction was agreed during a visit by President Vladimir Putin to North Korea in 2024.
The two countries' ties have grown stronger since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022 with Pyongyang sending thousands of troops to Russia's Kursk region to help repel a 2024 Ukrainian incursion there.
